subject: Next steps: marketplace vs PO for Acero — invoice format & net terms
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir@acero.ai>, Cara Lee <cara.lee@acero.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: marketplace vs PO for Acero — invoice format & net terms

Hi Samir / Cara —

Great to sync earlier. Quick recap and a few procurement/ops questions so we can lock the commercial path and get you an onboarding timeline:

Recap (short)
- You want Redwood for inference serving for Acero’s search-relevance feature (prod pilot -> limited rollout).
- Primary ask: predictable billing flow and legal/PO support.

Procurement & billing items we discussed (please confirm):
1) Commercial path: do you want to go through a marketplace (Azure/AWS) or direct PO to Redwood? Either works but the activation/timing and invoicing flow differ.
2) Net terms: what are your standard terms (Net 30 / Net 45 / Net 60)? We can offer standard Net 30; Net 60 requests require finance approval for enterprise contracts.
3) Invoice format: do you need machine-readable invoices (XML / UBL / PEPPOL) or a PDF with line items? If XML/e-invoicing, share the schema or we can map to your sample.
4) Billing address & tax: billing address for Acero, VAT ID (for EU reverse charge) or US EIN if applicable, and whether taxes should be shown on invoice.
5) PO number placement & AP email: we will include a PO field on all invoices if you provide the PO number and the AP billing email.

Attached: redwood-invoice-sample.xml and a short procurement-checklist.pdf to show fields we typically include.

Next steps I propose:
- Samir / Cara: confirm preferred path (marketplace vs PO), net terms target, and the AP billing contact + billing address + tax ID.
- Ben: will share two commercial options (marketplace flow vs PO-commit) and any pricing delta.
- Rishi / Legal: will prepare an optional PO-friendly SOW template if you pick direct procurement.

Happy to hop on a 15-min follow-up with procurement if that helps — let me know availability.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-invoice-sample.xml (stub), procurement-checklist.pdf (stub)

From: Samir Kapoor <samir@acero.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Cara Lee <cara.lee@acero.ai>, Acero AP <ap@acero.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: marketplace vs PO for Acero — invoice format & net terms

Thanks Naomi — useful recap. A few answers and follow-ups from our side:

1) Path: Procurement preference is to onboard via PO to Redwood (direct vendor) for this pilot. Marketplace is acceptable for proof of concept if it gets us running faster, but procurement will still want vendor paperwork on file.

2) Net terms: Acero typically operates on Net 60 for new vendors; we can do Net 30 sooner for strategic pilots but will need a three-person approval chain. Is Net 60 something Redwood can accommodate on a pilot contract?

3) Invoice format: Our AP team prefers an XML e-invoice with the following fields: PO number, invoice number, invoice date, GL code, cost center. I attached our AP requirements doc (Acero_AP_requirements.docx).

4) Billing details: Please show invoices to: Acero AI, 125 Market St, Suite 400, San Francisco, CA 94105. AP email for invoice submission: ap@acero.ai. Tax: Acero is US-based (EIN 94-1234567); we do not have EU VAT for this org.

5) Marketplace specifics: if we choose Azure Marketplace, we need clarity on how end-of-month billing and PO references flow through the marketplace. Can Redwood include a contractual addendum that explains the marketplace billing cadence?

On timing: procurement can sign a PO within 10 business days once we have a sample invoice mapping and confirmation of Net terms.

Cheers,
Samir Kapoor
Head of Platform Partnerships | Acero AI
samir@acero.ai

Attachment: Acero_AP_requirements.docx (stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir@acero.ai>, Cara Lee <cara.lee@acero.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: marketplace vs PO for Acero — invoice format & net terms

Thanks Samir — this is perfect and helps a lot. A few clarifications and our proposed path:

- Net terms: we routinely support Net 30. Net 60 is possible for enterprise accounts with finance sign-off; I will escalate immediately and flag this as an "enterprise exception" in our internal queue. Would you be able to accept Net 30 temporarily while we process the Net 60 approval? That would let the pilot start sooner.

- Invoice format: we can produce a native XML e-invoice containing PO number, invoice number/date, line-item breakdown, and custom fields (GL, cost center). I attached a lightweight e-invoice-schema.json to show field mappings we support. If you can point out any missing fields in your Acero_AP_requirements doc, we will map it.

- Billing address & tax: noted (125 Market St, Suite 400, San Francisco, CA 94105, EIN 94-1234567). We will include the EIN and blank VAT fields as applicable.

- Marketplace addendum: Ben will include a short note about marketplace billing cadence and the difference in how POs are referenced.

Immediate next steps from our side:
1) Ben to share two options (marketplace quick-start vs direct PO onboarding) with the expected timing and pricing delta.
2) I will open the Net 60 request and update by EOD tomorrow on whether finance approves for this deal.
3) If you confirm PO onboarding, please send the sample PO you will use so we can validate mapping.

If helpful I can put a 20-minute slot on calendar tomorrow morning for procurement + AP to iron this out.

Best,
Naomi

Attachments: e-invoice-schema.json (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir@acero.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: marketplace vs PO for Acero — invoice format & net terms

Samir — quick commercial note from my side. Two pragmatic options we recommend:

Option A — Marketplace fast-start (recommended for speed)
- Activation: same-day to 3 business days (marketplace listing dependent).
- Billing: marketplace issues the invoice; payment settlement follows marketplace cadence (we can provide transactional metadata so your AP can reference PO numbers).
- Pricing: small listing/fee delta (~3-5% premium compared to direct).
- Pros: fastest time-to-usage, minimal vendor paperwork up-front.
- Cons: less direct control over invoice layout; need marketplace to pass through PO fields.

Option B — Direct PO to Redwood (preferred for long-term control)
- Activation: 5-10 business days (legal + vendor onboarding + PO issuance).
- Billing: direct XML invoice to ap@acero.ai with PO number and EIN included.
- Terms: Net 30 standard; we can route Net 60 for enterprise deals subject to finance approval (this is what Naomi will escalate).
- Pricing: base pricing (no marketplace premium).

My ask: please confirm target timeline and whether you want us to start marketplace paperwork in parallel as a fallback. If procurement is willing to accept a temporary Net 30 while Net 60 is approved, we can start provisioning earlier.

I can include the marketplace addendum and a PO-friendly SOW in the next note; Naomi — should I attach both to the HubSpot deal so Acero can review?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
